_doc: Hand-placed covers for ebooks that resolve NEITHER a sibling audiobook cover NOR an embedded EPUB cover.
Read by scripts/build_ebook_manifest.load_cover_overrides() as cover source 3 (see that module's header).
WHY IT STORES AN OBJECT KEY, NOT A URL: the image is fetched ONCE, by a person, and staged under
site/covers/ebooks/<sha256>.<ext> exactly like an extracted EPUB cover, so the existing step 5.7
(scripts/upload_covers_r2.py) uploads it to the same R2 bucket and records it in site/covers_manifest.json.
The pipeline therefore makes NO network call to build the manifest, and a dead upstream link can never
blank a cover that is already in the bucket.
TO ADD ONE (two steps, deliberately manual):
1. Download the cover and write it to site/covers/ebooks/<sha256-of-the-bytes>.jpg
2. Add an entry below keyed on the ebook's `path` in site/ebooks.json, then rebuild the manifest and
This list should stay SHORT. A growing list means the automatic sources are failing and should be fixed
instead - which is exactly what happened on 2026-08-17, when 15 EPUBs looked coverless and were really
just being rejected for size (the fix was downscale_cover, not 15 override entries).

Ellen Javernick/What If Everybody Said T.why: Fixed-layout landscape picture book (comic-type EPUB): 14 interior images, no cover declared in the OPF and no sibling audiobook, so both automatic sources correctly return null. The ASIN is the EPUB's OWN dc:identifier (urn:asin:B078JR36SH), so the art is keyed to this exact edition rather than a guessed match. Verified by eye before staging: title, author and illustrator on the jacket all match.
Ellen Javernick/What If Everybody Said T.not_verified: openlibrary.org was unreachable from this machine and the Google Books API answered 429 on every retry (2026-08-17), so neither of those two sources could be consulted for a comparison.
